The successful state debt auction further bolstered market confidence. Despite new U.S. sanctions on Iran, traders stayed vigilant regarding potential supply issues in the oil sector. Throughout the day, strong liquidity levels contributed to resilience in the debt market.

Broader markets were mixed, while Pharma and PSU Bank stocks outperformed. HDFC Life, Cipla and ONGC were among the top Nifty losers.

title: Hindustan Copper OFS subscribed over 3 times; govt to exercise greenshoe option

title: Quote of the day by Walter Schloss: "Historically, many companies that have had terrible times have come back, or many of them do. A decline doesn’t mean it’s the end"
description: Walter Schloss urged investors to look beyond short-term stock declines and assess underlying business strength. Temporary setbacks can reverse when fundamentals remain intact, but investors must evaluate valuation, financial health, management, competitive advantages and long-term earnings potential before seeing weakness as opportunity.

title: House of Abhinandan Lodha ties up with NITCO for Alibag project, to invest Rs 1,000 cr
description: House of Abhinandan Lodha plans to allocate Rs 1,000 crore for its latest project in Alibag, which will feature a blend of apartments, townhouses, and a luxury hotel. This venture, marking their second initiative in the area, is anticipated to contribute greatly to the revenue streams of the involved real estate companies. Notably, NITCO has secured a deposit of Rs 9 crore from its collaboration partner.

title: Puravankara Ltd expects Rs 1,100 cr revenue from 8-acre housing project in Bengaluru

The company has secured a Joint Development Agreement for a prime 7.83-acre site, which will feature a saleable area of approximately 0.89 million square feet. With a robust portfolio of land holdings and ongoing projects nationwide, Puravankara continues to strengthen its position in the real estate market.

title: Inorbit Malls completes acquisition of 2 malls for Rs 1242.5 cr
description: Inorbit Malls has bolstered its presence by purchasing two additional malls from Prozone Realty for a hefty Rs 1,242.5 crore. This significant deal, which effectively doubles their asset portfolio to eight malls in just a year, encompasses properties in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore. Prozone Realty has acknowledged the successful transfer of equity shares in these assets, elevating Inorbit Malls' total leasing area beyond five million square feet.
